II
What then is the meaning of miracle from the standpoint
of the Christian religion? To what extent is Christian belief a
belief in miracles? At all events, miracle implies an action
wrought by God. To believe in miracle means, as we have
already suggested, to be prepared to believe that the miracu-
lous working of God meets us in our lives. It has often been
said that all events are essentially miraculous. For if we
believe in God as the Omnipotent, the Creator of heaven and
earth, we must also be persuaded that all things are trace-
able to His action and energy and that all that happens to us
is miraculous.
It is no doubt true that belief in God as Creator implies
that all events are ultimately the effect of His operation.
However, the situation is that the creative activity of God
remains hidden from us, that we do not always and every-
where recognize and experience Him as Creator. Normally
we view life and the world as an ordered state of things and as
a process of controlled happenings grounded in the law of
cause and effect. What takes place here springs partly from
the movement of nature which is regulated by laws that we
know, and whose forces we are more and more able to bring
within our control, and partly from the impulsion of the
human will and the planning of the human mind-things
which are also intelligible to us. Where then does the
miraculous creative action of God come into play?
There are no doubt moments in our lives when we believe
that we become aware of the guidance and government of
God the Creator; moments in which His miraculous action
strikes us with powerful impressiveness. Such moments
